This makes the developed country capital-abundant compared to the developing country, and makes the developing country labor-abundant compared to the developed country. questions.explanation: Heckscher Ohlin Model Assumptions The assumptions of the Heckscher-Ohlin model suggest that two countries exist, have similar technological structures and similar consumption tastes. We are assuming such a structure to simplify things in the model. It removes the possibility of trade without regard to technological differences and guarantees consumption of goods without any cultural differences. Traded goods can be produced based on two different factors. Our first factor is capital and second factor is labour, there exist two commodities with different structures of factors. Our first good, X, requires more capital to produce when we compare it to Y, which requires more labor to produce. One country is capital endowment and the other country is labor endowment. Heckscher-Ohlin's model assumes a perfectly competitive market where factors are constant between countries. This shows that workers from one country cannot migrate to another country. Similarly, companies in one country cannot transfer their assets to another country. The factors within countries are completely dynamic. This means that without any cost, the country can change its production structure and switch it to different combinations of factors.
